original_value: A framework of path planning for autonomous electric bus is presented. ArcGIS platform is utilized for map-building and global path planning. Firstly, a high-precision map is built based on GPS in ArcGIS for global planning. Then the global optimal path is obtained by network analysis tool in ArcGIS. To facilitate local planning, WGS-84 coordinates in the map are converted to local coordinates. Secondly, a double-layer finite state machine (FSM) is devised to plan driving behavior under different driving scenarios, such as structured driving, lane changing, turning, and so on. Besides, local optimal trajectory is generated by cubic polynomial, which takes full account of the safety and kinetics of the electric bus. Finally, the simulation results show that the framework is reliable and feasible for driving behavior planning and trajectory generation. Furthermore, its validity is proven with an autonomous bus platform 12 m in length.

result.paraphrase: A path-planning framework for an autonomous electric bus is introduced. It uses the ArcGIS platform for map creation and global route planning. First, a high-precision map is constructed from GPS data in ArcGIS for global planning, and the global optimum path is then derived using ArcGIS network analysis tools. To support local planning, the map’s WGS-84 coordinates are converted into local coordinates. Next, a two-layer finite state machine (FSM) is developed to plan driving behavior across different scenarios, including structured driving, lane changes, turning, and more. In addition, a local optimal trajectory is produced with a cubic polynomial, fully considering the safety and kinematics of the electric bus. Simulation results indicate that the framework is reliable and feasible for driving behavior planning and trajectory generation, and its validity is further demonstrated on a 12 m autonomous bus platform.
